title: Disposal of Infected Materials and Specimens
path: Disposal of Infected Materials and Specimens

headings.title: Principles of Infection Control and Waste Segregation
headings.content: Proper management of infected materials forms the bedrock of nosocomial infection prevention in Nigerian healthcare facilities. Every nurse bears professional and legal responsibility for ensuring that waste generated during patient care does not pose a hazard to colleagues, waste handlers, or the surrounding community. Infection control relies heavily on source reduction and immediate segregation at the point of generation. Mixing hazardous infectious waste with ordinary municipal refuse creates massive occupational risks and violates standard nursing protocols.

headings.title: Classification of Medical and Laboratory Waste
headings.content:
- **Infectious Waste**: Materials containing pathogens in sufficient concentration to cause disease, including cultures, stocks, and items contaminated with blood or body fluids.
- **Pathological Waste**: Human tissues, organs, body parts, and recognizable fetuses.
- **Sharps**: Objects that can puncture or lacerate skin, such as needles, scalpels, lancets, and broken glass.
- **Pharmaceutical Waste**: Expired, unused, or contaminated drugs and vaccines.
- **General Health-care Waste**: Non-hazardous office supplies, food packaging, and administrative refuse.

headings.title: Color-Coding and Segregation Guidelines in Nigeria
headings.content:
Adhering to national color-coding standards ensures uniformity across clinics and teaching hospitals in Nigeria. Standard guidelines dictate specific receptacle colors for distinct waste streams to minimize sorting errors.

| Receptacle Color | Waste Category | Examples |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Yellow / Brown | Infectious & Pathological | Soiled dressings, swabs, human tissues, blood bags |
| Yellow (Puncturable) | Sharps | Needles, syringes with fixed needles, blades |
| Black | General / Domestic | Food wrappers, office paper, non-contaminated debris |
| Red | Highly Infectious / Radioactive | Laboratory cultures, isolation ward waste |

headings.title: Safe Packaging, Transport, and Storage of Laboratory Specimens
headings.content:
Diagnostic specimens must be packaged securely using the **triple packaging system** to prevent leakage during transit from the ward to the laboratory. 
1. Primary receptacle: A leak-proof primary container holding the specimen itself.
2. Secondary packaging: A durable, leak-proof secondary container enclosing enough absorbent material to soak up all liquid if the primary container breaks.
3. Outer rigid packaging: A sturdy exterior box providing structural protection against crushing forces during transport.

Laboratory request forms should never be wrapped around the primary container; instead, place them in a separate exterior pouch to prevent contamination of patient data.

headings.title: Methods of Treatment and Decontamination
headings.content: Before final disposal, infectious waste often requires preliminary treatment to neutralize pathogens. **Autoclaving** uses pressurized steam to sterilize items effectively and remains the gold standard for laboratory cultures and reusable surgical goods. **Chemical disinfection**, typically utilizing sodium hypochlorite solutions, is applied to surfaces and liquid waste streams. Incineration is reserved for anatomical parts and high-risk infectious items that require complete structural destruction.

headings.title: Management of Accidental Spills and Exposures
headings.content: Despite strict safety protocols, needle-stick injuries and fluid spills occur in clinical settings. Nurses must act swiftly following an exposure incident. For percutaneous injuries, encourage bleeding under running water, wash the site with soap and water, and avoid scrubbing. Report the incident immediately to the infection control unit for risk assessment and potential post-exposure prophylaxis. For liquid biological spills on floors, confine the area, wear heavy-duty gloves, apply a chlorine-based disinfectant, allow adequate contact time, and clean the surface mechanically.
